  • for (preposition): 'For' is a preposition used to indicate a period of time, often used with the present perfect or past perfect tense, not directly after 'Did'.

The blank in the sentence 'He had an accident two weeks ________.' requires a word that correctly completes the time expression referring to the past. In English, we use 'ago' after a period of time to indicate how long before the present something happened.
  • since (preposition/conjunction): 'Since' is used to indicate the starting point of an action that continues to the present, not to refer to a finished period in the past.
